subject: Post-call: Novus discovery and hyperscaler gap triage
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan@novusanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Novus discovery and hyperscaler gap triage

Jordan —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed set of next actions so we can align on a focused eval: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost while preserving answer fidelity for search summarization and automated reporting pipelines.
- Pain points: hallucinations on long-context summarization, unpredictable token costs on peak loads, and lack of consistent latency across regions.
- Current stack: internal retrieval layer -> HyperscalerX hosted LLM endpoint (v1.2, 8k context) -> post-processing rules.

Redwood hypotheses for gap areas to test (high level)
1) Hallucination frequency on factual extracts vs HyperscalerX baseline (same prompts).
2) Token-cost delta when enabling prefix-KV caching + batching compared to baseline.
3) Tail latency under 99th percentile load (simulate 600 RPS spike).

Immediate next steps I suggest
- You share a 200–500 row sample (anonymized) of the summarization prompts and expected gold outputs by EOD Tue (we can accept a subset).
- We run 3 controlled comparisons: HyperscalerX baseline, Redwood default model config (8k), Redwood with KV caching + quantized weights.
- Deliverable: short report with hallucination rate, exact-match where applicable, token cost per request, and 95/99 latency.

If that works I’ll loop in Ben to scope the test matrix and Marissa for the eval deck and timeline.

Thanks,

—
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: call-notes-20270620.txt (stub)

From: Jordan Myers <jordan@novusanalytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novusanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Novus discovery and hyperscaler gap triage

Ava —

Thanks for the clear recap. Yes, that alignment matches our internal notes. We can provide an anonymized sample of ~300 rows by EOD Tue. A couple clarifications:

- For hallucination checks, can you run both your default sampling policy and a deterministic decode so we can see differences?
- On cost, we’d like a simple per-1k-requests projection based on our expected traffic (estimate in doc).

We’ll also include an internal compliance contact in the sample delivery so you have a single intake point.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Jordan
Jordan Myers
Director of Engineering | Novus Analytics
jordan@novusanalytics.com | +1 (617) 555-0188

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan@novusanalytics.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood test matrix + prompt set (first pass)

Jordan — looping in details on the tests we recommend and artifacts attached. I kept this tight to address your asks (deterministic + sampling outputs, hallucination metrics, cost projection).

What I attached
- novus_gap_tests.csv: rows mapping your sample IDs to prompt variants and expected gold output columns.
- eval_prompts_v2.txt: prompt templates for summarization, extractive QA, and report generation previews.
- redwood_test_matrix.xlsx: mapping of models/configs and metrics we’ll capture.

Proposed test plan (timeline in business days)
1) Day 0 (upon sample): quick sanity run (100 rows) to validate the pipeline and prompt formatting.
2) Day 1–2: Full runs against three cohorts: HyperscalerX baseline, Redwood-default, Redwood-with-caching+quant.
3) Day 3: Consolidate results, produce hallucination breakdown (by prompt type), cost model, and a short slide with recommended config.

Metrics we’ll report
- Hallucination rate (manual + automated heuristics)
- Exact-match / ROUGE-L for extractive items
- Token cost per request (projected per 1k requests)
- 95th/99th latency under synthetic spike

Open questions for you
- Will the sample include any PHI or regulated identifiers (if yes we need an NDA amendment before ingestion)?
- Do you have a preferred secret-sharing method for the Drive link (we can provide SSO-protected intake)?

If you’re good with this I’ll kick off provisioning the three test endpoints in our sandbox and share the results link.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0210

Attachments: novus_gap_tests.csv (stub), eval_prompts_v2.txt (stub), redwood_test_matrix.xlsx (stub)

Jordan —

Great — thanks for the confirmation and for sending the sample. We’ve provisioned three sandbox endpoints and I’ve dropped the eval runbook and intake folder to the Drive link below. Please upload the anonymized CSV to the "Intake/Novus_ANON" folder and add a short README with any edge-case flags (tokenization notes, expected truncation behavior).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNovus-Eval
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/RDW-2027-0893 (I added the test matrix and will log results there)

We’ll run the deterministic and sampling configs you requested and expect the first sanity run back within 24 hours of sample upload. If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min sync for Fri to walk through initial results.

—
Marissa Cole
